title: MedNeXt: Transformer-Driven Scaling of ConvNets for Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Fully ConvNeXt encoder-decoder with residual ConvNeXt up/down blocks and large depthwise kernels; UpKern initialises a large-kernel net from a trained small-kernel net, which avoids saturation on small data.
adaptation: 2D MedNeXt in nnU-Net at 512 px, 1 channel, label-safe augmentation. Train k3 first, then UpKern to k5/k7 to widen context along crack direction while keeping 1 px detail in the full-resolution stage.
min_experiment: MedNeXt-B k3 then UpKern k5 on the module-grouped folds, against the ResEnc M arm on the same folds; metric CV-mean crack relF1@2 and E1 relF1@2. Kill: no fold-mean gain above 1 fold SD on either.
evidence: R: best on 5 of 6 3D datasets in nnU-Net Revisited (for example ACDC 92.65, BTCV 85.04 against 83.08 org), at 68 to 233 A100 h in 3D. Part of the gain was explained by target spacing choice.

alt_notes.adaptation: 2D MedNeXt-B/L k3 at 512 px, 1 channel, label-safe aug, then UpKern to k5. Large kernels give context for E1 (scuff v crack) without attention. 2D support in repo unverified; a 2D port of the block is small.
alt_notes.min_experiment: MedNeXt-B k3 and k5 (UpKern) 2D, 5 folds v nnU-Net arm A. Metric: CV crack relF1@2, inactive IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill if no metric improves by >=0.01 (CV) or 0.03 (E1).
